title: Symmetry of the finite forward compact-support external product
statement:
Use the finite-coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$, and ordinary constant-$A$ derived categories on the small pro-etale sites. Let $B,X,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $f:X\to B$ and $g:Z\to B$ be separated finite type, and put $P=X\times_B Z$, with projections $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Z$ and $h=fp=gq$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the concrete chosen-compactification exchange and forward projection transformations of [def-exchange-projection], and the normalized compact-support composition comparisons $\alpha$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Let $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $N\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be equipped with etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. Assume that every tensor object in the following composite and in the composite with $(f,M)$ and $(g,N)$ exchanged is bounded below and of etale origin. In particular require this of $Rf_!M\otimes_A^L Rg_!N$ and $Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N$. All tensors and symmetries are the specified derived sheaf tensor and its signed symmetry [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Define the forward product $\Xi_{f,g}(M,N)$ to be exactly
$$
\begin{aligned}
Rf_!M\otimes_A^L Rg_!N
&\xrightarrow{\sigma}Rg_!N\otimes_A^L Rf_!M
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,Rf_!M}}Rg_!(N\otimes_A^L Lg^*Rf_!M)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rg_!(\sigma)}Rg_!(Lg^*Rf_!M\otimes_A^L N)
\xrightarrow{Rg_!(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}\otimes1)}Rg_!(Rq_!Lp^*M\otimes_A^L N)\\
&\xrightarrow{Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{q,Lp^*M,N})}Rg_!Rq_!(Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N)
\xrightarrow{\alpha_{g,q}}Rh_!(Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N).
\end{aligned}
$$
For the swap $s:P\xrightarrow{\sim}Z\times_BX$, let $S$ be the canonical identification from $R(g\times_B f)_!(N\boxtimes M)$ to $Rh_!(M\boxtimes N)$ obtained from the scheme isomorphism $s$ and the tensor symmetry $Lq^*N\otimes_A^L Lp^*M\to Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N$. Here $M\boxtimes N=Lp^*M\otimes_A^L Lq^*N$ and the swapped notation has the corresponding meaning. Then the actual forward maps satisfy
$$\Xi_{f,g}(M,N)=S\circ\Xi_{g,f}(N,M)\circ\sigma_{Rf_!M,Rg_!N}.$$
No constructibility, finite Tor amplitude or invertibility of the projection transformations is assumed; the stated bounded-below etale-origin conditions are retained. No exceptional functor or abstract six-functor datum is an input.

proof.text: Use the compactifications already chosen in the definition of the two forward maps, writing $f=aj$, $g=bk$. Put $H=j_!M$, $J=k_!N$, $F=Ra_*H$, $G=Rb_*J$, and $C=\bar X\times_B\bar Z$, with $r,t,c,u,D$ as in [lem-pur-finite-product-compactification]. That lemma identifies the actual map $\Xi_{f,g}$ with $Rc_*(e)\Omega_{a,b}(H,J)$, and identifies the exchanged actual map with the analogous expression for $(b,a,J,H)$. Its hypothesis about tensor objects holds in each order by the hypotheses of this item. The lemma includes transport from the independently chosen compactifications of the intermediate maps, so this is an equality of the specified maps, rather than a replacement by an arbitrarily chosen product morphism. It remains to compare the two proper composites and their open tensor identifications.

proof.text: The open comparison $e$ used in Step 1 intertwines signed symmetry. Indeed factor $u$ as $P\xrightarrow{w}X\times_B\bar Z\xrightarrow{v}C$. Open base change expresses $Lr^*j_!M$ as $v_!$ of the pullback of $M$; the tensor comparison for $v$ puts the other factor inside $v_!$. On $X\times_B\bar Z$, open base change of $k$ and the tensor comparison for $w$ then give $u_!D$. The opposite factorization gives the analogous isomorphism. By [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] each open comparison restricts to the identity under the open units. Both maps are therefore maps between objects in the essential image of the fully faithful $u_!$, with the same restriction, so are equal. The same test applied to the square obtained by swapping the factors and inserting tensor symmetry gives a commutative square: both restricted composites are exactly $\sigma_{Lq^*N,Lp^*M}$. Compatibility of pullback with signed symmetry is [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. This proves the required symmetry of $e$, including all Koszul signs.

proof.text:
Compute the proper composite on $C$. Put $E=Lr^*H\otimes^LLt^*J$ and let $x:Lb^*F\to Rt_*Lr^*H$ be ordinary exchange. Its transpose is $Lr^*(\varepsilon_{a,H}):Lt^*Lb^*F\cong Lr^*La^*F\to Lr^*H$ by the definition in [def-exchange-projection]. Let $v=\pi_{t,Lr^*H,J}\circ(x\otimes1_J)$. Under $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$ its transpose, using the tensor comparisons, is
$$\widehat v=(\varepsilon_{t,Lr^*H}\otimes1)\circ(Lt^*x\otimes1)=Lr^*\varepsilon_{a,H}\otimes1_{Lt^*J}.$$
The first equality is exactly the counit definition of $\pi_t$ and naturality of the tensor comparison; the second is the defining transpose equation for $x$. No exchange or projection is inverted.

proof.text:
Write $w=Rb_*(\sigma_{J,Lb^*F})\circ\pi_{b,J,F}\circ\sigma_{F,G}:F\otimes^LG\to Rb_*(Lb^*F\otimes^LJ)$. Its $Lb^*\dashv Rb_*$ transpose is
$$\widehat w=\sigma_{J,Lb^*F}\circ(\varepsilon_{b,J}\otimes1)\circ\sigma_{Lb^*F,Lb^*G}=1_{Lb^*F}\otimes\varepsilon_{b,J}.$$
Here $G=Rb_*J$. The first equality is the definition of the ordinary projection transformation. The second is naturality and involutivity of signed symmetry; pullback carries the input symmetry to the displayed one by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. All maps, including counits, have degree zero, so this calculation introduces no extra sign.

proof.text:
The ordinary proper product is $\Omega_{a,b}=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}\circ Rb_*(v)\circ w$. Transpose successively under $Lb^*\dashv Rb_*$ and $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$, with the canonical composite adjunction $Lc^*\dashv Rc_*$. The composite hom bijection is the one of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] supplies its pasting normalization. The compositor $\kappa_{b,t}$ of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] is the conjugate of the pullback compositor $Lc^*\cong Lt^*Lb^*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]: for constant $A$ the inverse images are exact, the module sheaf categories are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheaves-grothendieck], and [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] identifies the conjugate of the derived pullback compositor with the class of the termwise sheaf compositor on K-injectives, which is the normalization of $\kappa_{b,t}$. Hence transposing $\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}$-composites under $Lc^*\dashv Rc_*$ is transposing successively under $Lb^*\dashv Rb_*$ and $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$. Naturality of each hom bijection gives
$$\widehat\Omega_{a,b}=\widehat v\circ Lt^*(\widehat w)
=(Lr^*\varepsilon_{a,H}\otimes1)\circ(1\otimes Lt^*\varepsilon_{b,J})
=Lr^*\varepsilon_{a,H}\otimes Lt^*\varepsilon_{b,J}.$$
Its source is $Lc^*(F\otimes^LG)\cong Lr^*La^*F\otimes^LLt^*Lb^*G$ and target is $E$. The direct-image compositor is [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]; the pullback tensor and composition identifications are those of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The last equality is functoriality of tensor [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial].

proof.text:
Repeat Steps 3--5 for $(b,a,J,H)$. Identify $\bar Z\times_B\bar X$ with $C$ by the swap. After precomposing with $\sigma_{F,G}$ and postcomposing with the external tensor symmetry, its transpose becomes
$$\sigma_{Lt^*J,Lr^*H}\circ(Lt^*\varepsilon_{b,J}\otimes Lr^*\varepsilon_{a,H})\circ\sigma_{Lr^*La^*F,Lt^*Lb^*G}
=Lr^*\varepsilon_{a,H}\otimes Lt^*\varepsilon_{b,J}.$$
This is naturality and involutivity of the same signed symmetry; compatibility of its pullback and the factor-swap identifications is [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Direct images respect transport along the swap by [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition]. The adjunction hom bijection is injective, so the two proper forward morphisms themselves agree under these input and output symmetries.

proof.text: Apply $Rc_*$ to the commutative open-comparison square of Step 2 and combine it with the equality of proper maps in Step 6. Substitute the two factorizations from Step 1. The swap of the product compactifications restricts to $s:P\to Z\times_BX$; its external tensor symmetry followed by the open comparison is therefore exactly the map used to define $S$ in the statement. Thus the substituted equality is $\Xi_{f,g}(M,N)=S\circ\Xi_{g,f}(N,M)\circ\sigma_{Rf_!M,Rg_!N}$. The comparison lemma applies on precisely the bounded-below etale-origin tensor domain assumed here. None of Steps 2--6 required boundedness of the auxiliary ambient tensor objects or invertibility of any projection map.
